summary.text: A 74-year-old man with COPD, benign prostatic hyperplasia, hepatitis C carriage and recurrent NSCLC with bone and pleural metastasis (cT4N0M1c) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and left lower lobectomy was admitted in August 2024 with voiding difficulty. He had recent pembrolizumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin chemotherapy, palliative C7 radiation, a chemoport placed 37 days before admission, prior drug-induced immune-mediated colitis probably caused by nivolumab, and ongoing S. boulardii probiotics.

Initial vital signs were blood pressure 107/66 mmHg, pulse rate 100 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.4 C and pulse oximetry 98% on room air; WBC was 3.51 x 10^9/L, CRP 7.77 mg/dL, kidney and liver function tests were within normal limits, and chest CT showed no interval change in left pleural thickening or the left upper lobe mass.

On hospital day 2 he developed watery diarrhea without fever, with WBC 29.83 x 10^9/L and CRP 27.1 mg/dL; C. difficile toxin B PCR and toxin A+B antigen were positive. Meropenem and oral vancomycin were prescribed; diarrhea and CRP improved, with Acinetobacter nosocomialis in one aerobic culture set on day 6.

Because CRP rose to 4.94 mg/dL, blood cultures on day 12 were followed by identification of S. cerevisiae on day 15 (MALDI-TOF MS score 2.0; 18S rRNA 100% match). Micafungin for 4 days was followed by fluconazole 400 mg per day for 22 days; subsequent cultures on days 15 and 19 still grew the organism, the chemoport was removed on day 21 with S. cerevisiae >15 CFU on the tip culture, and the probiotics were discontinued.

Blood cultures on day 24 showed no growth, there was no fever during treatment, WBC was within the reference interval and CRP 1.9 mg/dL at the end of treatment, the bloodstream infection resolved after catheter removal, and C. difficile colitis did not recur during 6 months of follow-up after discharge. Susceptibility testing done after treatment gave fluconazole MIC 32 ug/mL (high), caspofungin 0.25 ug/mL and flucytosine <=1 ug/mL; voriconazole and amphoterin B were not assessed.
